messages:
sam_csm: FYI customer ACME reporting their embeddings changed shape after they pinned to our 'stable-2026-02' alias. Downstream index failing due to wrong dim.
acme_integration: Confirming — before pin we got 1024-length vectors. After pin swap yesterday (~2026-02-18 10:12 UTC) we see 1536. Indexer throws shape mismatch. No other changes on our side.
jasper_support: Thanks — can you paste the raw response headers and the model field from the embeddings response?
acme_integration: Here's the curl we used and a trimmed response:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \ 
  -d '{"model":"stable-2026-02","input":["hello world"]}'

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Redwood-Model: openembed-1b@v3
X-Embedding-Dim: 1536
Content-Type: application/json

{ "model": "openembed-1b/pin:v3", "embedding_len": 1536, "embedding": "[...1536 floats...]" }
```
deploy-bot: variant-freeze: alias stable-2026-02 -> openembed-1b@v3 (applied by ci-pipeline at 2026-02-18T10:11:54Z)
liang_eng_ml: Quick look: openembed-1b@v2 had dim 1024; v3 is 1536. It looks like the alias was pointed at v3 during the freeze. Likely a tagging mismatch in the deployment that used 'latest' for the pinned alias. I'll check registry and rollout history.
jasper_support: Can you also check request logs for the exact model param the customer sent? We need to confirm whether the alias resolved server-side to the v3 artifact.
liang_eng_ml: Confirmed in our routing logs: alias stable-2026-02 resolved to openembed-1b@v3 for requests between 2026-02-18T10:11:50Z and 2026-02-18T10:13:00Z due to a CI tag race. We're preparing a remap to point the alias back to openembed-1b@v2. ETA ~30m.
jasper_support: For mitigation, support can offer a temporary server-side compatibility shim: truncate/pad embeddings to 1024 for this customer until alias is remapped. Will need approval from eng for a quick patch. @liang_eng_ml possible?
liang_eng_ml: I can push a lightweight shim in the routing layer that truncates to requested dim when model family supports it. Patch will be behind a customer flag. Deploying to edge in ~20m.
sam_csm: I'll ask ACME if they're ok with truncation (note: may impact quality). They said they prefer immediate unblock over emedding fidelity.
acme_integration: Ok to try truncation for now — please proceed and we'll validate with our indexer.
liang_eng_ml: Patch deployed to canary at 3965432120, then rolled to production at 3965432140. Alias remap to openembed-1b@v2 also completed at 3965432140.
jasper_support: Can you re-run the same curl and paste headers again after 3965432140?
acme_integration: Re-ran test at 3965432150. Response:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Redwood-Model: openembed-1b@v2
X-Embedding-Dim: 1024
{ "model": "openembed-1b/pin:v2", "embedding_len": 1024, "embedding": "[...1024 floats...]" }
```
acme_integration: Verified our index accepts the vectors now. Thanks! :tada:
jasper_support: Root cause: CI deploy step used non-deterministic 'latest' tag when generating alias mapping which allowed v3 (1536 dim) to become the alias target. Fix: pin deploy scripts to explicit artifact digests; add pre-freeze dim check as a gating test.
liang_eng_ml: Filed PR to CI with digest pinning + a check that alias target embedding_dim matches expected. Also added a one-off audit to find other aliases that might point to mismatched artifacts.
sam_csm: Noted. I'll follow up with ACME summary and link to incident. Great cross-team work.
acme_integration: Appreciate the quick turnaround — thanks everyone.
